The period of the wave is 91 ms.
What can be determined about the wave?
A
It has a velocity of 0.44 m s–1 and a frequency of 11 Hz.
B
It has a velocity of 0.55 m s–1 and a wavelength of 5.0 cm.
C
It is longitudinal and has a frequency of 11 Hz.
D
It is transverse and has a wavelength of 4.0 cm.

hints: Look at the distance / cm axis and find two successive points in the same state of motion, such as crest to crest from 0 to 4.0 cm, to get wavelength.
Recall $f = 1/T$ with $T = 91\text{ ms} = 0.091\text{ s}$ and $v = f\lambda$ to link the given period to frequency and speed.
Ask whether a displacement against distance snapshot tells you if particle vibration is along or across the direction of energy transfer.
walkthrough: Read wavelength $\lambda$ from the displacement-distance graph. A crest occurs at $0$ and the next crest at $4.0\text{ cm}$, with a full trough between, so $\lambda = 4.0\text{ cm} = 0.040\text{ m}$.
Calculate frequency from the given period $T = 91\text{ ms} = 0.091\text{ s}$ using $f = 1/T$. So $f = 1/0.091 \approx 11\text{ Hz}$.
Calculate wave speed using $v = f\lambda$. So $v \approx 11 \times 0.040 = 0.44\text{ m s}^{-1}$, with units of distance over time.
Note that longitudinal versus transverse depends on oscillation direction relative to propagation direction, which is not shown by this snapshot of displacement versus distance.
Therefore the determinable pair is $v = 0.44\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $f = 11\text{ Hz}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Wavelength is $4.0\text{ cm}$ and $f = 1/T \approx 11\text{ Hz}$, so $v = f\lambda \approx 0.44\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: Wavelength is $4.0\text{ cm}$, not $5.0\text{ cm}$, because crests repeat from $0$ to $4.0\text{ cm}$ on the distance axis.

C.explanation: Frequency of $11\text{ Hz}$ is correct but a displacement-distance graph does not show whether oscillations are parallel or perpendicular to travel.

D.explanation: Wavelength of $4.0\text{ cm}$ is correct but transverse cannot be determined from this graph alone.
